message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, sorted roughly by passenger traffic (largest to smaller but still significant):

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger numbers; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; home to many international carriers. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Large hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-site airports worldwide. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Known for its distinctive peaked roof; hub for United and Southwest Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for many airlines including JetBlue and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Key hub for flights to Asia and the Pacific Rim; known for its efficient layout. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta; known for its “rainy” weather. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for flights to Latin America and the Caribbean; key for American Airlines. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando, FL | MCO | Major hub for travelers to theme parks; hub for Southwest Airlines. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | Hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports in the U.S. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) | Charlotte, NC | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the busiest airports on the East Coast. |
| George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) | Houston, TX | IAH | Major hub for United Airlines; known for its large cargo operations. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) | Newark, NJ | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; serves the New York metropolitan area. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) | Washington, DC | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; serves the nation's capital. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger traffic, flight movements, and cargo throughput. They also serve as major hubs for their respective airlines and provide extensive domestic and international connections.
